short: A 2022 US law that funds domestic semiconductor manufacturing to reduce reliance on foreign, mostly Asian, chip production.
definition: The CHIPS Act (formally the CHIPS and Science Act, passed in the United States in 2022) is a law that provides tens of billions of dollars in subsidies and incentives to build semiconductor factories on American soil. Its goal is to reduce US dependence on chips made overseas — especially in Taiwan and South Korea — which are essential to everything from phones to the GPUs that power AI. It reflects the wider push for compute sovereignty: a country deciding that the ability to make its own advanced chips is too strategically important to leave to other nations. Several other regions have since launched similar chip-subsidy programs.
